tool.name: LoCoHFixedSphere
tool.summary: Fixed-sphere-of-influence (r-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) home-range and utilization-distribution estimator (Getz et al. 2007).
tool.usage:
Choosing r. The radius r sets the size of each point's "sphere of influence." Larger r gives larger, smoother hulls; smaller r gives tighter, more fragmented hulls. At least the focal point and its two nearest neighbours are always included, so every hull forms a polygon.
Getz et al. (2007) suggest, as a starting heuristic, r equal to half the maximum nearest-neighbour distance (the default option here), then refining toward the value that minimizes the combined Type I and Type II error via the "minimum spurious hole covering" (MSHC) rule (Getz and Wilmers 2004). The T-LoCoH R package (Lyons, Turner and Getz 2013) recommends choosing the parameter empirically by examining how isopleth area and spurious holes change across a range of values.
When you specify a radius, it may be entered in any linear unit and is converted to meters internally. Screen out obvious location errors before running, as LoCoH is sensitive to outliers.
References: • Getz and Wilmers (2004) Ecography 27:489-505, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.0906-7590.2004.03835.x • Getz et al. (2007) PLoS ONE 2(2):e207, https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000207 • Lyons, Turner and Getz (2013) Movement Ecology 1:2, https://doi.org/10.1186/2051-3933-1-2
Environments. This tool honors the Output Coordinate System environment. If it is set to a coordinate system other than the input's, the output polygons are reprojected to it as a last step; areas, point counts, densities, and within-sphere counts remain computed in the input coordinate system. No other geoprocessing environments affect this tool.

dialogReference.para: The point features (for example, GPS or VHF telemetry fixes) from which the local hulls are built. May be in a geographic or projected coordinate system; empty or null geometries are ignored.

param.name: r_method
param.expression: Automatic (half the maximum nearest-neighbor distance) | Specify a radius

dialogReference.para: How the sphere radius r is determined. Automatic (half the maximum nearest-neighbor distance) sets r to the Getz et al. 2007 r1 heuristic. Specify a radius enables the Radius parameter so you can enter a value.
The sphere radius r, used only when Specify a radius is chosen. Enter a value in any linear unit; it is converted to meters for the computation. The radius used is recorded in the output metadata.

Output polygon feature class of the dissolved cumulative LoCoH isopleths. Each feature stores its dissolved area (Area), enclosed point count (Point_Count), point proportion (Point_Proportion), the number of points within the sphere (Sphere_Point_Count), and point density in points per square kilometer (Pts_per_SqKm).
Optional output polygon feature class of the individual local convex hulls, each with its own area, point count, proportion, within-sphere point count, and point density.

scriptExample.title: LoCoH (Fixed Sphere) example
scriptExample.para: Run a fixed-sphere LoCoH using the automatic radius (half the maximum nearest-neighbor distance), creating the cumulative isopleths and the individual hulls.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages arcpy.jenness.LoCoHFixedSphere( "Owl_6_Points", "Automatic (half the maximum nearest-neighbor distance)", None, r"C:\Project\HomeRanges.gdb\Owl_6_Points_FixedSphere_Cumulative", r"C:\Project\HomeRanges.gdb\Owl_6_Points_FixedSphere_Hulls")

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Fixed-sphere-of-influence (r-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) home-range and utilization-distribution estimator (Getz et al. 2007).
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Estimates an animal's home range and utilization distribution using the fixed-sphere-of-influence (r-) Local Convex Hull (LoCoH) method of Getz et al. (2007). For every input point, the local hull is the convex hull of that focal point and all points within a sphere of influence of radius r, always including at least the focal point and its two nearest neighbours. Hulls are sorted by point count (most first) and merged cumulatively into density isopleths, each attributed with its dissolved area, enclosed point count and proportion, the number of points within the sphere, and point density (points per square kilometer). The radius r can be set automatically to half the maximum nearest-neighbour distance (the Getz et al. 2007 r1 heuristic) or specified in any linear unit, which is converted to meters for the computation. Distances use the Haversine formula for geographic data and planar distance converted to meters for projected data. The primary output is the dissolved cumulative isopleths; an optional second output contains the individual hulls. Method reference: https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0000207
